activity.list.description: What runs for a workspace and would stop if it closed.

activity.stop.description: Stop some of what runs for a workspace (for example everything AI asked for); each is ended for real.

ai.call.description:
(An AI client inside TALYX) call an action as AI, in a workspace. The platform runs it and records the call; whether to ask the
user first is the AI client's decision, from the action's effects.

ai.calls.description: Recent recorded calls by AI and running code.

ai.catalog.description:
List modules with their AI guide summaries and authoring docs. Supply a module to read its AI actions, effects,
inputs and examples.
When nextCursor is present, pass it as cursor with the same module to continue.

ai.guide.description:
Read a module's Markdown guide, or with topic one of its authoring docs: how to write code the module runs
(where the files go, the API, how to save and check them). ai.catalog lists each module's docs. Continue with
nextCursor.

catalog.implementations.description: Implementations of an extension point by enabled modules.

changes.list.description: List objects changed by your recorded calls or a code run in this workspace and conversation.

changes.revert.description: Restore the objects changed by one of your calls to their state before the call (undo) or after it (redo).

modules.definitions.description: Every installed module's manifest, contract and state, for the window to load module frontends.

modules.disable.description: Stop and disable a module. Refused while another enabled module requires it.

modules.enable.description: Enable a module and start it.

modules.install.description:
Install a module from a folder or a zip file, prepare its Python environment if it needs extra packages,
and start it.

modules.list.description: Installed modules, whether each is enabled and running, and why one could not start.

modules.reload.description: Regenerate a module's contract from its code and restart only that module.

modules.uninstall.description: Stop and remove an installed module and its environment.

notifications.channels.description: The user's push channels (Telegram, Feishu, Discord); credentials are never returned.

notifications.configure.description: Add, change or delete a push channel (the user only).

notifications.read_delivery.description: How a notification this module sent was delivered, per channel.

notifications.send.description: Send a notification on configured channels. Delivery is durable and retried; read_delivery reports it.

notifications.test.description: Send a test message on one channel and wait (up to 25 s) for its receipt.

notifications.toast.description: Show a Windows toast (unavailable where Windows cannot show one).

panels.activate.description: Bring a panel of the workspace's window to the front.

panels.capture.description: Capture a laid-out panel in its desktop workspace window. Returns a PNG file reference kept for 24 hours.

panels.close.description:
Close a panel in the workspace window. A busy panel can refuse with conflict; declining its confirmation
returns cancelled. The panel stays open in both cases.

panels.list.description: Panels in the workspace's window, with what each reports it shows.

panels.open.description:
To open a module, call platform.panels.open with {"type": "module.panel"} using the exact type listed below.
For a particular object, use platform.panels.open_target with module, panelType (the part after the dot)
and the object's openTarget objectId.

panels.open_target.description: Open an object in its module's panel (an open target, such as one object of that module).

runs.calls.description: The calls one run made (its starter only).

runs.end.description: The run is over: its token stops working.

runs.start.description:
A token for one run of code this module starts: the run's calls are recorded as code from this module and
workspace, and the context reaches the handlers it calls unchanged.

secrets.configured.description: Whether one of the calling module's secrets is set.

secrets.get.description: One of the calling module's secrets. Backends only: windows and AI learn whether one is configured.

secrets.set.description: Store (or with null, delete) one of the calling module's secrets.

settings.read.description:
Settings as they apply in a workspace (its own value, else the global one, else the default), or the global
ones with workspaceId "global".

settings.reset.description: Make a workspace follow the global value again for these settings.

settings.write.description: Set settings globally or for one workspace only. Global-only settings cannot be set for a workspace.

storage.directories.description: The calling module's data directory and user folder.

tasks.get.description: A long task's state, progress and, once finished, its result or error.

tasks.start.description: (Module SDKs) record a long task of one of the caller's task actions.

workspace.close.description:
Close a workspace: everything running for it (listed by activity.list) is stopped first, for real. A workspace
never saved is deleted as workspace.delete deletes one.

workspace.copy.description:
Copy a saved workspace, open or not: the copy is saved with the same layout under the name given (or
"<name> copy"), and each module copies what it keeps for the workspace. The copy gets its own copy of the folder
TALYX made for the workspace; a folder the user bound is shared, not copied. The copy is not opened.

workspace.delete.description:
Delete a saved workspace (with the revision read, so a newer save is not lost).
What the modules keep for it is deleted; the folder TALYX made for it goes to the Recycle Bin, one the user bound
stays.

workspace.delete_preview.description: List what deleting this workspace would remove: the modules' contents, then the folder TALYX made for it.

workspace.folder.description: The workspace's folder: its files, which modules read directly.

workspace.list.description: Saved workspaces, most recently saved first.

workspace.list_open.description: Open workspaces, most recently opened last.

workspace.open.description: Open a workspace: a new one, one by its workspaceId, or a saved one by snapshotId; the window shows it.

workspace.save.description:
Save the calling workspace's state (the window's layout and panels) under a name; a workspace has one saved
state, saved over with snapshotId and the revision read. Saved from no workspace, it is a new workspace's.

workspace.set_folder.description: Bind the workspace to an existing folder (the user's choice), or back to its own.

workspace.shown.description: (The window) which open workspace this window shows and how many panels of each module it holds.

activity.changes.description: Read activity.list on the first item, then again when work starts, ends or changes in a workspace.

modules.changes.description: Modules being installed, enabled, disabled, started, restarted or failing; read modules.definitions again.

notifications.activated.description: The user clicked a toast that leads somewhere.

settings.changes.description: Settings that changed (a global change is reported once with workspaceId "global").

workspace.changes.description: Workspaces opening, closing and being copied, from now on.

workspace.windows.description: Every open workspace with the window showing it: now, then again whenever that changes.

activity.ended.description: Registered background work ended in its workspace.

notification_section.description: A module's section of the notification settings.

settings_section.description: A section of the settings window drawn by a module's view.

status_item.description: An item in the window's status bar.

upColor.title: Up color
upColor.description: Which color means up for prices, P&L, buy and sell, everywhere in TALYX.

launchOnLogin.title: Start TALYX when you sign in
launchOnLogin.description: Works in the TALYX desktop app.

keepAwakeWhileWatching.title: Keep the computer awake while work is running
keepAwakeWhileWatching.description: Only while an open workspace has work running. The screen can still turn off. Works in the TALYX desktop app.

client.description: Which AI client is calling (a module acting as AI client, or an external client's name)
client.title: Client

target.description: Input field naming the object an action without effect branches acts on.
target.title: Target

summaryPaths.description: Output paths to vocabulary Summary values; * selects array elements.
summaryPaths.title: Summarypaths

ActivityRef.description: One activity: its id is the module's own, so the module is part of who it is.
ActivityRef.title: ActivityRef

docs.description: Authoring docs: how to write code the module runs; read one with ai.guide {module, topic}.
docs.title: Docs

configured.description: Whether its credentials are stored (they are never read back).
configured.title: Configured

credentials.description: Left out to keep the stored ones.

chatId.description: Telegram only: the chat the bot writes to.
chatId.title: Chatid

userDir.description: The module's folder among the user's files
userDir.title: Userdir

environmentsDir.description: The Python environments every module shares (the SDK's uv tool keeps them there, with who holds each)
environmentsDir.title: Environmentsdir

modulesDir.description: Where the modules the user installs or writes live; a module folder made here is installed where it is
modulesDir.title: Modulesdir

title.description: What the document helps the reader write.
title.title: Title

topic.description: One of the module's authoring docs (ai.catalog lists them); without it, the module's guide.
topic.title: Topic

path.description: A folder holding talyx.module.json, or a zip file of one
path.title: Path

LayoutSummary.description: Each panel's module and its place, as shares of the workspace: a saved workspace's thumbnail.
LayoutSummary.title: LayoutSummary

pid.description: Process ID of the connected module interpreter, or null when disconnected.
pid.title: Pid

contract.description: public/contract.json, generated from the module's code
contract.title: Contract

assetBase.description: Where the module's files are read (its frontend entry is under it)
assetBase.title: Assetbase

pid.description: Process ID of the connected module interpreter, or null when disconnected.
pid.title: Pid

panel.description: A panel type of the sender (``module.panel``).
panel.title: Panel

view.description: The module's own view (its name in the manifest's views).
view.title: View

notificationId.description: Chosen by the sender; sending the same id and content again is answered with the first delivery.
notificationId.title: Notificationid

workspaceId.description: An open workspace to show again, or a closed one to open again under its id.
workspaceId.title: Workspaceid

snapshotId.description: A saved workspace: the workspace it is a saved state of opens again.
snapshotId.title: Snapshotid

presentation.description: What the window keeps for the workspace while it is open (its unsaved layout).
presentation.title: Presentation

view.description: What the panel reports it shows (its module's own words), if it reports anything.
view.title: View

conversation.description: The AI conversation this code acts for: its changes can be listed and undone from that conversation
conversation.title: Conversation

url.description: Where the process sends its calls (TALYX_CALL_URL)
url.title: Url

workspace.description: The window's layout and panel states (at most 4 MB).
workspace.title: Workspace

snapshotId.description: Save over this saved workspace (with the revision read); left out for the first save.
snapshotId.title: Snapshotid

module.description: The module whose settings these are ("platform" for General)
module.title: Module

view.description: The module's own view (its name in the manifest's views) drawn as the section.
view.title: View

workspace.description: Also show this section in This workspace and pass the selected scope to the view.
workspace.title: Workspace

moduleInstances.description: How many panels of each module the window holds.
moduleInstances.title: Moduleinstances

action.description: The module's window action run when it is clicked.
action.title: Action

navigation.description: Where clicking it leads (notifications.activated reports the click).

target.description: Input field naming the object an action without effect branches acts on.
target.title: Target

summaryPaths.description: Output paths to vocabulary Summary values; * selects array elements.
summaryPaths.title: Summarypaths

sessionId.description: The window showing it, if one does.
sessionId.title: Sessionid

WorkspaceChange.description: A workspace opened, closed, was copied, or had its saved state written or renamed.
WorkspaceChange.title: WorkspaceChange
